extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and practitioners working on clickbait detection, explainability, dataset construction, and evaluation of text classification/attribution models
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, evaluating, and releasing an interpretable benchmark and models for detecting clickbait headlines and attributing them to specific linguistic manipulation strategies. Includes synthetic dataset creation, a two-stage modelling framework (detection then tactic attribution), and comparisons of fine-tuned classifiers vs large language models under different prompting regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explainable / interpretable clickbait detection
rubrics_metrics.description: A model for explainable clickbait detection that not only identifies clickbait titles but also attributes them to specific linguistic manipulation strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises interpretability/explainability as a deployment requirement: detection models should provide human-understandable explanations linking a headline to manipulation tactics rather than opaque binary labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tactic attribution to linguistic manipulation strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute clickbait headlines to specific linguistic manipulation strategies (i.e., predict which persuasive tactics are present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The second stage uses a dedicated BERT-based classifier to predict the specific clickbait strategies present in each headline; outputs should map to a predefined catalogue of tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage analysis framework (detection then tactic attribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: A two-stage framework for automatic clickbait analysis comprising detection and tactic attribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate the pipeline into (1) identifying whether a headline is clickbait, and (2) predicting which tactics are used. Designs and evaluations should reflect this modular decomposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthetic dataset generation via systematic augmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A synthetic dataset generated by systematically augmenting real news headlines using a predefined catalogue of clickbait strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset construction should be systematic: start from real headlines and apply controlled augmentations according to an explicit catalogue of tactics so that each example's manipulative strategy is known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled experimentation and detailed analysis enabled by dataset
rubrics_metrics.description: The synthetic dataset enables controlled experimentation and detailed analysis of model behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Datasets should be constructed to support fine-grained, controlled experiments (e.g., isolating single tactics, comparing tactic combinations) and allow detailed behavioral analyses rather than only aggregate metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model comparison across architectures and prompting regimes
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare a fine-tuned BERT classifier with large language models (LLMs), specifically GPT-4.0 and Gemini 2.4 Flash, under both zero-shot prompting and few-shot prompting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation must include multiple model classes (fine-tuned discriminative models vs LLMs) and consider different inference strategies (zero-shot vs few-shot) to assess relative strengths and weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompting strategy: zero-shot and few-shot with illustrative examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Use both zero-shot prompting and few-shot prompting enriched with illustrative clickbait headlines and their associated persuasive tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating LLMs, include experiments that supply exemplars (few-shot) consisting of headlines paired with tactic annotations to assess whether examples improve detection/attribution and interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource sharing / dataset availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Share the dataset with the research community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarks should be released openly so others can reproduce experiments, extend analyses, and compare methods under the same controlled conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and trustworthiness as overarching goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance the development of transparent and trustworthy AI systems for combating manipulative media content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should prioritize transparency (clear datasets, interpretable model outputs) and the broader goal of building systems that improve credibility and user trust in digital media.
